blocks.content: An article without which this Constitution would be a nullity... It is the very soul of the Constitution and the very heart of it.

rows: Enforces Fundamental Rights as well as ordinary legal rights
Applicable throughout the entire territory of India
Confined to the state territory or where the cause of action arises
Is itself a Fundamental Right (SC cannot refuse relief)
Is a discretionary power (HC may refuse to exercise writ power)

items: Article 32 can be invoked exclusively for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights, whereas Article 226 applies to both Fundamental Rights and legal rights.

The Supreme Court cannot refuse to exercise its writ jurisdiction under Article 32 because the remedy itself is a Fundamental Right, whereas High Court jurisdiction under Article 226 is discretionary.
Habeas Corpus is the only writ that can be issued against both public authorities and private individuals.
Mandamus cannot be issued against private individuals, the President of India, or State Governors.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 32 confers the right to remedies for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights guaranteed under Part III of the Constitution.
Dr. B.R. Ambedkar famously referred to Article 32 as 'the very soul of the Constitution and the very heart of it'.
The five constitutional writs available under Article 32 are Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari, and Quo-Warranto.
The Supreme Court's power to issue writs under Article 32 is part of the basic structure of the Constitution and cannot be abridged by constitutional amendments.
The right guaranteed by Article 32 cannot be suspended except as provided for by the Constitution during a declared National Emergency under Article 359.
